chunks: 4213 - And ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī narrated from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام that he said:
I asked him about that over which invocation was made for other than Allah, so he said:

"Whatever is slaughtered for an idol, image, or tree, Allah has forbidden that just as He has forbidden carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine. 'But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then there is no sin upon him' to eat carrion."
He said: So I said to him, O son of the Messenger of Allah, when does carrion become lawful for the compelled one? He said:

"My father narrated to me from his father, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked, and it was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, we may be in a land and famine strikes us, so when does carrion become lawful for us? He said: 'So long as you do not take a morning meal, or an evening meal, or gather herbs, then you may resort to it.'"
ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm said: So I said to him, O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:
۝ But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then there is no sin upon him ۝

He said: "The transgressor is the thief, and the rebellious one is he who seeks hunting out of insolence or amusement, not so as to bring it back to his dependents. It is not permitted for either of them to eat carrion when they are compelled. It is forbidden to them in the state of necessity just as it is forbidden to them in the state of choice. And it is not permitted for them to shorten fasting or salat (prayer) in travel."
He said: So I said: then His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:
۝ The strangled, the beaten, the fallen, the gored, and that which a wild beast has eaten, except what you properly slaughtered ۝

He said: "'The strangled' is that which was strangled by its throat until it dies. 'The beaten' is that which became ill and disease cast it down until no movement remained in it. 'The fallen' is that which falls from a high place to below, or falls from a mountain or into a well and dies. 'The gored' is that which another beast strikes with its horns and it dies. 'That which a wild beast has eaten' is that from which it ate and it died. 'That which is slaughtered on stone altars' means on a stone or idol, except what is caught while its proper slaughter can still be performed, so it is duly slaughtered."
I said: "And that you seek division by arrows?"

He said: "In the pre-Islamic period, they used to buy a camel among ten persons and divide it by casting arrows. They were ten: seven had allotted shares and three had no shares. As for those that had shares, they were al-Fadh, al-Taw'am, al-Nafis, al-Hils, al-Musbil, al-Mu'alla, and al-Raqib. As for those that had no shares, they were al-Safih, al-Manih, and al-Waghd. They would circulate the arrows among the ten, and whoever had one of the arrows without shares come out in his name was charged one-third of the camel's price. They would continue in this way until the three arrows without shares fell upon three of them, and they would obligate them with the camel's price. Then they would slaughter it, and the seven who had contributed nothing to its price would eat it, while the three who had paid its price would eat nothing from it. When Islam came, Allah, Exalted is His mention, prohibited that among what He prohibited, and He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ۝ And that you seek division by arrows; that is grave disobedience ۝ meaning unlawful."

key_terms.أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِ: That over which invocation was made for other than Allah, making it forbidden.
key_terms.غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ: Without rebellious intent or transgression beyond lawful necessity.
key_terms.ٱلنُّصُبِ: Stone altars or idols upon which animals were slaughtered.
key_terms.ٱلْأَزْلَامِ: Divining arrows used for allotment and gambling-like division.
key_terms.ٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ: An animal fatally struck down or rendered lifeless.
key_terms.ٱلْمَيْتَةَ: Carrion, an animal that died without proper slaughter.
key_terms.ٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ: An animal that dies by strangulation or suffocation.

ai.seo_question: What does the Qur'an mean by forbidden carrion, necessity, and seeking division by arrows?
ai.summary: This hadith explains several Qur'anic rulings about forbidden foods, necessity, and the meanings of specific terms in the verses on slaughter and carrion. It also clarifies who may not invoke necessity as an excuse and describes the pre-Islamic practice of division by arrows that Islam prohibited.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4213 - Abdul Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Ridha (as), peace be upon him:
I asked Imam (as) about what has been sacrificed for other than Allah (swt).

Imam (as) said: "Whatever is slaughtered for an idol, a statue, or a tree, Allah (swt) has forbidden it, just as He (swt) has forbidden carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine.
'But if one is forced by necessity, without willful disobedience nor transgressing due limits, then there is no sin upon him' to eat from the carrion."
I then asked Imam (as): "O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), when does carrion become permissible for one who is compelled by necessity?"

Imam (as) said: "My father (as) narrated to me from his father (as), from his forefathers, peace be upon them all, that the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, was asked: 'O Messenger of Allah (swt), we may find ourselves in a land where we are struck by severe hunger. When does carrion become lawful for us?'
Prophet (sw) said: 'As long as you have not had a morning or evening meal, or found herbs to sustain yourselves, then you may consume it.'"
Abdul Azim said: I asked Imam (as): "O son of the Messenger of Allah (swt), what is the meaning of Allah's (swt) statement:
'But whoever is forced by necessity, neither desiring it nor transgressing its limits, then there is no sin upon him' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:173)

Imam (as) said: "The 'transgressor' (al-ʿadi) is the thief, and the 'oppressor' (al-baghi) is the one who hunts out of arrogance or for amusement, not to provide sustenance for his dependents. Neither of these two is permitted to eat carrion in a state of necessity. It remains forbidden for them in times of necessity just as it is forbidden in times of ease. Likewise, they are not allowed to shorten their prayers or fasts during travel."
I then asked Imam (as) about Allah's (swt) statement:

'And (forbidden to you is) that which dies by strangling, and that beaten to death, and that which dies from falling, and that which is gored, and that which a wild beast has eaten-except what you are able to slaughter properly.' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3)
I then asked about Allah's (swt) statement:

'And (forbidden is) that you seek division by arrows.' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3)
Imam (as) said: "During the pre-Islamic era (Jahiliyyah), people used to buy a camel collectively, shared among ten individuals. They would then divide its shares using arrows. There were ten arrows, seven with shares and three without shares.
As for those with shares, they were: 'al-Fadh' (the single), 'al-Taw'am' (the twin), 'al-Nafis' (the valuable), 'al-Hils' (the covering), 'al-Musbil' (the extended), 'al-Mu'alla' (the elevated), and 'al-Raqib' (the watcher).
Those without shares were: 'al-Safih' (the wasteful), 'al-Manih' (the granted), and 'al-Waghd' (the despicable).
They would cast lots among the ten participants. Whoever's name came up with one of the three arrows without shares had to pay one-third of the camel's price. They would continue this process until the three arrows without shares fell to three individuals, obliging them to pay for the camel.
Then they would slaughter the camel, and the seven who paid nothing would eat from it, while the three who paid for it would neither eat from it nor benefit in any way.
When Islam came, Allah (swt) Almighty prohibited this practice as part of what He (swt) forbade. Allah (swt) said:
'And (forbidden is) that you seek division through arrows. That is disobedience.' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3)
This means it is unlawful."
